doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: (laughs) Anybody else that you’d like to play with or not?
I don’t know. Just about anybody, I guess, that… I’d like to, to do some gigs with Gary Larson sometime. That should be fun. Yeah. I think that, that’s about it
Any compositions in your head? Like I would like to write a ballet or…
Not really. I wouldn’t mind writing another orchestra piece or finishing the one that didn’t get finished.

Unfinished symphony, right. That’s good. I don’t really know, Deb. I’m just, just kinda taking it a day at a time and a note at a time, and with any luck, moving forward in increments, is that the right term?
Okay. Just looking to see if there’s anybody else that I wanted to ask you about that we didn’t get to but… we covered a whole lot of ground.
Yeah, I know it. I can’t believe you had all that. I feel like, feel like I’ve been spied upon.
This is way off the subject but you know that guy got murdered right down the block.
Is that…? The guy who had been in a wheelchair and…
Yeah, we even talked about Jimmy Raney and…
…Attila. We got a lot of people in there.
